useCase.name: Put the admission inquiry form on the website, and take it down when the school is not taking inquiries
useCase.featureRef: 28.2 Publishing and removing the online inquiry form

routesElsewhere.goesTo: No intent. The public inquiry form only — UC-02-01, which is not planned.
routesElsewhere.note: A family fills the form themselves at the public address, with no login and no session to plan against. Nothing in this layer submits on their behalf, because the submission is stamped as coming from the website and that stamp would then be false.

request.gloss: I want to look at the inquiries that have come in

request.gloss: let the form open by itself on 1 January

routesElsewhere.note: There is no scheduling. The form is up or it is down, because a family either can apply or cannot (BR-8, E6).

request.text: sirf Johar Town campus ke liye form kholein
request.gloss: open the form for the Johar Town campus only

routesElsewhere.note: One school-wide state as modelled. Whether the form should be publishable per branch where a school has several campuses is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-2).

routesElsewhere.request: put a notice on the site saying admissions are open
routesElsewhere.note: A notice is an item somebody writes. The form is a state somebody sets, and the two are separate acts.

steps.note: One step, and it takes no parameters beyond the branch: the form is up or it is down, and there is nothing in between to configure (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where the website cannot be reached nothing changes and it is reported, rather than the form appearing to have been published (BR-7, E3, AC-7).
plan.atomicity: One state change and one outbound call, together. Either the form is on the site or it is not — a state recorded as published that no family can see is the failure this use case exists to prevent.

operations.name: website.inquiryform.publish
operations.idempotencyKey: the inquiry form has one state, so a repeat is the same publication rather than a second one (E4)
operations.purpose: Put the inquiry form on the school website.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Whether the form is on the site, and from when.

fields.name: on_the_site
fields.description: True. Families can complete it (BR-3).

fields.name: published_by
fields.description: Who put it up, recorded by name (BR-5).

fields.name: published_on
fields.description: From when. This is what a school asked why no inquiries came in a month has to be able to read (BR-5, A4).

fields.name: public_url
fields.description: Where the form now stands, completed with no login (BR-3).

fields.name: closed_message_cleared
fields.description: True. The message saying inquiries are closed comes down as the form goes up (BR-8, A1).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
errors.note: The right is the same website permission the Super Admin grants (BR-1, AC-1).

errors.meaning: The form is already on the site.
errors.note: The state is what it was asked to be, so nothing is wrong — but a second row in the history would make it look as though admissions reopened on a day they did not.

errors.meaning: The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: The form is not on the site and its state is unchanged.
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to have taken effect (BR-7, AC-7).

planningRules.rule: Never treat publishing the form as announcing that admissions are open. The form on the site lets a family who finds it apply; it tells nobody. A notice is a separate act, and a message to existing families is another.
Never offer to schedule it. There is no partial state, no scheduling and no per-class control, because a family either can apply or cannot (BR-8, E6).

Say that it is one state for the whole school. Whether the form should be publishable per branch is an open question the use case raises and does not answer, so a request naming one campus is answered plainly rather than quietly applied to all (OQ-2).
Report an unreachable website as nothing changed. A school that believes the form is up stops watching for the inquiries that are not arriving (BR-7, E3, AC-7).

reversal.statement: The form comes down again, and taking it down needs the message the page will show in its place (BR-4, E2). Inquiries received while it was up are unaffected either way (BR-6, AC-6).

request.text: naye session ke liye admission form website pe laga do
request.gloss: put the admission form on the website for the new session

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin holding the website permission, Johar Town branch. The form is currently down.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the form is up from today and the closed message has come down. Add what publishing does not do: it announces nothing. A family who does not visit the site will not know admissions have opened, and telling them is a notice or a message, both separate acts.

request.text: form pehle se laga hua hai kya? phir bhi publish kar dein
request.gloss: is the form already up? publish it anyway

resolvedPlans.context: Staff member holding the permission, with the form already on the site.

steps.note: The call reports it as already published rather than recording a second one (PR-1 is about announcement; the repeat is handled by the operation itself).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that it is already on the site and has been since the date it went up — and that nothing was recorded, because a second row would read as though admissions reopened on a day they did not. That date is what the school reads later when it asks why the inquiries stopped.

intent.name: website.inquiryform.remove
intent.summary: Take the inquiry form off the website, and say on the page why. Never a dead page.
routesHere: take the inquiry form down, we are full

routesHere.text: inquiry form website se hata do, ab admissions band hain
routesHere.gloss: take the inquiry form off the website, admissions are closed now

routesHere.text: form band kar dein aur page pe likh dein ke January mein dobara khulega
routesHere.gloss: close the form and put on the page that it reopens in January

request.text: form mein ek naya khana add karna hai
request.gloss: I want to add a new field to the form

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing about the form's fields is decided here. This use case controls only whether the form is on the site (BR-2, AC-9).

request.text: jo inquiries aayi hain unhein dekhna hai
request.gloss: I want to look at the inquiries that have come in

routesElsewhere.note: Working through inquiries received is the admissions module's. This use case only decides whether more can arrive.

request.text: form hata do lekin page khali chhod do
request.gloss: take the form down but leave the page empty

routesElsewhere.note: The page says plainly that inquiries are closed. A page showing nothing, or a form that fails on submission, tells a family nothing and loses them (BR-4, E2, AC-5).

request.text: jo inquiries aa chuki hain wo bhi hata do
request.gloss: remove the inquiries that have already come in too

routesElsewhere.note: A submission already made is unaffected by the form coming down. An inquiry received is an inquiry that must still be answered (BR-6, AC-6).

request.text: class bhar jane par form khud band ho jaye
request.gloss: let the form close by itself when a class is full

routesElsewhere.note: Nothing closes the form automatically. Whether it should close when a class reaches capacity is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-3).

steps.note: One step. The form comes off and the closed message goes up in its place — the two are the same act, because a page with neither is the failure the rule exists to prevent (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. With no closed message the form is not removed (E2), and where the website cannot be reached nothing changes and it is reported (BR-7, E3).
plan.atomicity: One state change and one outbound call, together: the form off the page and the message on it. Every inquiry already submitted is untouched (BR-6, AC-6), including one submitted in the moment the form came down (E5).

operations.name: website.inquiryform.remove
operations.idempotencyKey: the inquiry form has one state, so a repeat is the same removal rather than a second one
operations.purpose: Take the inquiry form off the site and put the closed message in its place.

parameters.name: closed_message
parameters.notes: What the page says while the form is down, in the school's own words. Required (BR-4, E2, AC-4) — this is what a family reads instead of applying, and whether it invites them back is the school's to decide.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What came down, what the page says now, and what survived it.

fields.name: on_the_site
fields.description: False.

fields.name: removed_by
fields.description: Who took it down (BR-5).

fields.name: removed_on
fields.description: When. A school asked why it received no inquiries in a month reads this (BR-5, A4).

fields.name: closed_message
fields.description: What the page now says, in the school's words (BR-4).

fields.name: days_up
fields.description: How long the form stood before it came off.

fields.name: submissions_while_up
fields.description: How many inquiries arrived in that period. They are unaffected and still have to be answered (BR-6, AC-6).

errors.meaning: The form was removed with no closed message.
errors.notWritten: The form stays on the site.
errors.note: A page showing nothing tells a family nothing and loses them (BR-4, AC-4).

errors.meaning: The acting user does not hold the right to publish to the website.
errors.notWritten: The form stays on the site.

errors.meaning: The school website could not be reached.
errors.notWritten: The form is still on the site and its state is unchanged.
errors.note: Reported rather than appearing to have taken effect (BR-7, AC-7).

planningRules.rule: Never write the closed message. It is what a prospective family reads instead of applying, and whether it invites them back in January or says nothing more is the school's decision, not a planner's (BR-4, OQ-1).

Never take the form down without one. There is no state where the page shows nothing — a family who finds an empty page or a form that fails on submission is a family the school has lost without knowing (BR-4, AC-5).
Say that inquiries already received are unaffected. An inquiry received is an inquiry that must still be answered, and closing the form does not close them (BR-6, AC-6).
Never suggest scheduling the closure or tying it to a class filling up. Neither exists: the form is up or it is down (BR-8, E6), and whether capacity should close it is an unanswered question (OQ-3).

reversal.statement: The form goes back up and the closed message comes down (A1, BR-8). Nothing about the period it was down is erased — the history keeps it, which is what a school reads when it asks why March was quiet (BR-5).

request.text: form band kar dein, ab jagah nahi hai, aur page pe likh dein ke January mein dobara khulega
request.gloss: close the form, there is no room now, and put on the page that it reopens in January

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin holding the website permission, Johar Town branch, form up for 74 days.

inputs.closed_message: as they gave it — inquiries reopen in January

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the form is down, what the page now says, and that the 148 inquiries received while it was up are untouched and still have to be answered. Say too that a family may be completing the form at this moment — a submission made against a live form is accepted, so one more may still arrive.

request.text: form hata do
request.gloss: take the form down

resolvedPlans.context: Staff member holding the permission, form currently up.

steps.note: No plan is emitted. The message is required and is not ours to write (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing comes down. Ask what the page should say — a prospective family who arrives to an empty page has no reason to come back, and whether the school invites them to return in January is the school's own decision.

operations.name: website.inquiryform.read
operations.purpose: Return whether the inquiry form is currently on the site, and what has arrived through it.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The state, who set it and what it has produced.

fields.name: on_the_site
fields.description: Whether a family can apply right now (BR-3).

fields.name: since
fields.description: When it was last put up or taken down.

fields.name: set_by
fields.description: Who did it (BR-5).

fields.name: closed_message
fields.description: What the page says while it is down. Empty while it is up (BR-4).

fields.name: submissions_this_period
fields.description: How many inquiries have arrived since the form last went up (BR-6).

fields.name: public_url
fields.description: The address a family reaches, with no login (BR-3).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the website forms screen.

planningRules.rule: Answer with the state and the date together. "The form is down" and "the form has been down since 15 February" are different answers, and only the second explains a month with no inquiries (BR-5, A4).
Give what the page says while the form is down. A family reading it is the school's only communication with them at that moment, and a school rarely remembers what it left there (BR-4).
Never read the state as whether the school has places. The form being up means a family can apply; it says nothing about capacity, and nothing closes it when a class fills (OQ-3).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kya abhi inquiry form site pe laga hua hai?
request.gloss: is the inquiry form on the site right now?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Answer with the state and since when, and with what the page says if it is down. Where it is up, say how many inquiries have come in since it went up — that is the number that tells the school whether the page is working at all, and it is not on the screen they asked about.

resolvedPlans.context: School Admin, Johar Town branch, form down since 15 February.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Say it is down, since when, who took it down and what the page tells a family who arrives. Add the part that matters and is not asked: inquiries received before it came down are unaffected and still have to be answered.

intent.name: website.inquiryform.history.read
intent.summary: Show when the form was up and when it was down, who changed it, and how many inquiries each period brought.

request.text: kaunsi inquiries aayi thi us dauran?

routesElsewhere.note: How many arrived in a period is here. Who they were and what became of each is the inquiry review's (BR-2).

routesElsewhere.note: A different record. The form's history explains the absence of inquiries; the items list explains what the site was saying.

steps.note: One read of an append-only record — one row per publication and one per removal (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A period nobody named is asked about rather than assumed, since "last year" and "the last twelve months" give different answers about a form that came down in December.
plan.atomicity: A read. The record is append only: a publication or a removal adds a row and never rewrites one (BR-5).

operations.name: website.inquiryform.history.read
operations.purpose: Return every publication and removal of the inquiry form, with what each period brought.

parameters.name: from_date
parameters.notes: The start of the period asked about.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: When the form was up, when it was down, and what each period produced.

fields.name: periods
fields.description: Each stretch the form was up or down: from, to, who set it, and the closed message where it was down.

fields.name: days_up
fields.description: How many days the form stood in the period asked about.

fields.name: days_down
fields.description: How many it did not. This is the answer to a quiet month (A4).

fields.name: submissions_by_period
fields.description: How many inquiries arrived in each stretch the form was live (BR-6).

fields.name: total_submissions
fields.description: Across the whole period asked about.

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the form history.
errors.note: The history screen is open to the School Admin, the Principal and the Super Admin.

planningRules.rule: Answer a quiet month with the state of the form first. A school asking why no inquiries came in March is usually asking about its advertising, and the answer is often that the form was down and somebody took it down (BR-5, A4).
Give inquiries against days up, not as a bare total. Forty in a month the form was live for eight days is a different fact from forty in a full month, and the bare number reads as the second (BR-6).
Never treat a period with the form down as a period with no demand. Nobody could apply — the page told them to come back, and how many read it and did not is not recorded anywhere (BR-4, OQ-4).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads cannot be edited by anybody, which is why it settles the question.

request.text: March mein koi inquiry kyun nahi aayi?
request.gloss: why did no inquiry come in March?

steps.note: The period is taken from the question and stated back (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Answer with the form's state through March: down from 15 February, taken down by the School Admin, with the page telling families to come back in January. Nobody could apply — so the month says nothing about demand, and how many families read that page and went elsewhere is recorded nowhere.

resolvedPlans.request: how many days was the form live last year, and what did it bring?

steps.note: The dates are stated back before the answer, since a form that came down in December makes "last year" and "the last twelve months" different questions (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the stretches it was up, the days in each and the inquiries each brought — not one total. A period with the form down is not a period with no demand, and the two read the same in a single number.
